C-CI-LINT-AND-PLAN-SHAPE-1-3526D6F0.Summary: Close three defects on three surfaces in one bundle: the repository's own governance lint runs in no CI job, so a markup, MODULE_MAP or graph-anchor defect reaches main with CI green (F284); the anchor-miss rule has no existence branch, so every plan that declares a not-yet-created module-ownable src/ file is red from approval until the task lands (F297); and `bun run test:metrics` runs the whole suite, so a bundle that regenerates `test-metrics.json` executes the suite twice (F299). The remedies are an explicit assertions-off lint mode plus a root governance lint inside `validate:ci`, an existence branch that warns on a declared-but-absent module-ownable path and keeps the error once it exists without an owning LINKS, and a metrics artifact derived from the single suite run `validate:ci` already makes.
C-CI-LINT-AND-PLAN-SHAPE-1-3526D6F0.Problem:
Three recorded findings [verified], re-measured 2026-09-19 at fead8a082646ecbe18e669981833ddcf4661d75f on branch c-ci-lint-and-plan-shape.
F284 — no governance lint in CI. `bun run validate:ci` invokes no `ngrace lint` in any form (`node -e` over package.json's `validate:ci` reports no `ngrace lint` and no `grace.ts lint` substring), and `.github/workflows/validate.yml` runs no lint step. The escape was observed, not hypothesised: executing C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016, five new exports across `src/gates/ledger.ts` and `scripts/test-affected.ts` landed without their MODULE_MAP entries, `bun run validate:ci` exited 0 over that tree, and the defect surfaced only when the executor ran the lint by hand. Measured this pass: planting an export without its MODULE_MAP entry makes `--assertions current`, `baseline`, `target` and `final` all exit 1 with `markup.module-map-mismatch`; a clean tree is 0/0.
The counterweight is a shipped ruling, and any remedy must answer it. Default assertion mode is `current` (`src/grace-lint.ts:89`), which evaluates the BaselineAssertions of every active approved plan. Measured this pass with an active approved plan carrying one BaselineAssertion that fails on the present tree: `--assertions current` exits 1 with `assertion.MustNotExist`, and `--assertions final` also evaluates unrelated active baselines. C-REPORT-HONESTY (archived) holds that the hazard of a current-mode lint is "a stale baseline masquerading as post-write evidence", `validate:examples` is acceptable only because it lints a different root, and `ngrace-plan`'s command rule forbids a current-mode lint of this root in `TargetAssertions`. A root `ngrace lint` added to `validate:ci` today would evaluate this project's active baselines mid-flight.
What the tool does not offer is an honest third mode. Measured this pass: with no `--change`, `--assertions baseline` and `--assertions target` both exit 1 with `assertion.change-required`, and `--assertions final` evaluates unrelated active baselines. There is no mode that runs markup, MODULE_MAP, graph-anchor and artifact-pure rules while evaluating no assertion at all. The finding names three shapes — a selected-assertion lint bound to no active change, a lint restricted to markup and graph rules with assertion evaluation off, or a check that runs only when no bundle is active. Making a selected-assertion mode legal without `--change` would contradict the shipped rule that every selected-assertion command names `--change` (F253 / C-TEACH-PLAN-DRIVES-CORRECTIONS-2), so this spec takes the second shape: a new explicit mode, `none`, that evaluates no BaselineAssertions and no TargetAssertions in any tree.
F297 — the anchor rule has no existence branch. `validateGraphAnchorsOwnWriteScope` (`src/lint/core.ts:750`) builds `linksByPath` from the governed-file records and requires, for every module-ownable ObservedWriteScope path, that the file's header LINKS a GraphAnchors module. A file not yet written has no record, so `links === undefined`, `owned` is false, and the error fires. Archived precedents C-INSPECTION-SURFACE-1-2628AA2B, C-APPLY-VERB and C-SUPERSEDE-VERB all declared a brand-new `src/` file in ObservedWriteScope and were red from approval until the file landed. Re-measured this pass on a throwaway copy: an active approved plan declaring `src/nonexistent-probe-xyz.ts` exits 1 with exactly one `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` and no other issue. The decision that created it, per the repository's own rule, is C-GRAPH-COVERAGE (A53) plus D12, which authorized the window and required it to be recorded rather than avoided. D12's argument is that an expected error named in advance is not a surprise; F297's counter-argument is that a rule known to fire on a correct artifact trains the reader to skip it. This spec does not weaken A53: ownership stays LINKS-only, archives stay unevaluated, and a file that exists without an owning LINKS still errors.
F299 — the metrics regeneration runs the suite a second time. `bun run test:metrics` spawns the whole suite (`scripts/test-metrics.ts:92`, `spawnSync("bun", ["test", "--timeout=0", "--reporter=junit", ...])`) to write `test-metrics.json`; a bundle that adds a test file must regenerate because the freshness guard (`scripts/test-metrics.test.ts`) compares the artifact's file list and count sum against a freshly computed tree walk, and the close's `bun run validate:ci` runs `bun run test` again. Timed this pass on a throwaway copy: `bun run test` 74.39 s, `bun run test:metrics` 74.80 s, combined 149.19 s for one metrics-regenerating bundle. The two numbers measure different things and the guidance conflates them: the full CI-equivalent invocation runs once (`validate:ci`), while the whole suite executes twice. The one-suite-run property of `validate:ci` is itself pinned by `validateCiRerunsSuite` (`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts:308`), created by C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016, so any tool remedy must change that predicate deliberately and keep its intent — each test file executes exactly once. The artifact also carries a per-file `ms` and a `generated` date, so an unconditional regeneration would churn on every run — every close commits timing noise and every developer run dirties the tree. The remedy therefore regenerates only when the freshness predicate says the committed artifact is stale (the file list or the count sum differs from a freshly computed tree walk) and leaves it byte-identical otherwise.

Goals.Goal: An explicit assertions-off lint mode exists: `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --assertions none` is accepted, reports `assertionMode` as `none` in `--format json`, runs every non-assertion rule the standard lint runs (markup, MODULE_MAP, graph-anchor ownership, scope, artifact validity), and evaluates no BaselineAssertions and no TargetAssertions in any tree — active or archived, selected or unselected. `current` remains the default and its behaviour is unchanged.

`validate:ci` runs a root governance lint that cannot evaluate a stale baseline: `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --assertions none --fail-on errors` is a member of the `validate:ci` chain. The planted F284 escape (an export without its MODULE_MAP entry) makes that member exit non-zero with `markup.module-map-mismatch`, and a clean tree with no active bundle is 0/0. The workflow needs no new step; it already calls `bun run validate:ci` (`.github/workflows/validate.yml:22`), and the Windows job's own steps are unchanged.

The anchor-miss rule has an honest existence branch. A module-ownable ObservedWriteScope path that does not exist on disk reports `change.graph-anchors-pending-file` at warning severity, naming the path and stating that the error applies once the file exists; the existing `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` error still fires when the path exists and its LINKS share no GraphAnchors module. The new code is registered in `src/lint/catalog.ts` with an `ngrace lint --explain` guide and is covered by the emitted-code scan.

`ngrace-plan`'s must_do row 6 stops teaching the transient as an unconditional error and names both states: a declared-but-absent module-ownable path warns `change.graph-anchors-pending-file` until the task creates the file, and the error `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` applies to a file that exists without an owning LINKS. The edit is forced, not cosmetic: the row's current sentence — that a not-yet-created path "errors `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` at every lint mode until the task that creates it lands" — is false the moment F297 lands. The canonical skill and its packaged mirror move byte-identically, the taught-rule token table follows, and the SKILL.md footprint pin and the README measurement cell it cross-checks are re-measured and transcribed.

A metrics-regenerating bundle executes the whole suite once and a bundle that adds no test file leaves `test-metrics.json` byte-identical. The single suite run in `validate:ci` emits its JUnit report to a temp path; before deciding to write, the stale check reads the committed `test-metrics.json`, computes the tree walk the freshness predicate names (`scripts/test-metrics.test.ts:31–33`), and regenerates the artifact from that report only when the file list or the count sum differs; when the artifact is fresh the derivation is skipped and the committed bytes are untouched. There is no second `bun test`. This requires `validate:ci` to use the JUnit-emitting suite runner as its one suite segment and `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts`'s one-suite-run predicate (`validateCiRerunsSuite`, `:308`) to accept that runner while still proving exactly one suite segment and no second `bun test`. `test-metrics.json` stays in the write scope because it moves when a bundle adds a test file, and it is excluded from every byte-invariance pathspec with that reason.

On this repository after the change, `bun run validate:ci` exits 0 on the applied tree; `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --assertions none --fail-on warnings` is 0/0 on the applied-archive tree; and no archived bundle is edited.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T2 (cross-cutting: the lint engine, the CLI surface, the release/CI surface, the metrics tool, the skill teaching surface and the packaged mirror). Roadmap RM-GOVERNED-PATH. Base commit fead8a082646ecbe18e669981833ddcf4661d75f, the fead8a0 merge. One bundle by the maintainer's ordering; the three findings do not split.

Anchors, in every list the artifact enumerates modules. `src/lint/core.ts` and `src/grace-lint.ts` declare `LINKS: M-LINT-CORE`; `src/lint/types.ts` declares `LINKS: M-LINT-TYPES` (the `LintAssertionMode` union is the new mode's home); `src/lint/catalog.ts` declares `LINKS: M-LINT-CATALOG`; `scripts/test-metrics.ts` declares `LINKS: [M-RELEASE-AUTOMATION, V-M-RELEASE-AUTOMATION]`; the canonical `skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` and its packaged mirror are `M-SKILLS`. `package.json`, `.github/workflows/validate.yml`, `README.md`, `test-metrics.json` and the `*.test.ts` files are not module-ownable and declare no anchor. The module list must agree wherever it appears.

The F284 remedy answers C-REPORT-HONESTY rather than overturning it. `none` evaluates no baseline, so no stale baseline can masquerade as post-write evidence; it is honest in CI and on a pull-request branch with an active approved plan. `current` keeps its default status and its baseline evaluation; no existing mode's meaning changes. Do not add a current-mode lint of this root to any `TargetAssertions`.

The F297 remedy does not overturn C-GRAPH-COVERAGE / A53 or D12's authorization. It answers D12 by making the transient named rather than silent: the declared-but-absent state gets its own code at warning, the file that exists without an owning LINKS still errors, archives are still not evaluated, and ownership is still LINKS-only, never a directory prefix. The pending warning is the state between plan approval and the creating task; at close every declared file exists, so `--fail-on warnings` sees no pending code.

The F284 and F297 remedies interlock by design. `change.graph-anchors-pending-file` is a warning and the CI lint runs `--fail-on errors`, so an active plan that declares a not-yet-created module-ownable file mid-execution does not red CI; this repository opens its pull requests after the close, when the file exists. The close's own `--fail-on warnings` lint (the `AC-CLOSE-LINT` shape, evaluated post-archive) sees nothing from this rule at all, because `validateGraphAnchorsOwnWriteScope` scans active scopes only and the bundle is archived by then.

Pinned surfaces move deliberately and are named. `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` holds `validateCiRerunsSuite` (`:308`) and `findUntrackedFixtureReads` (`:250`); `scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts` and its test hold the `ngrace-plan` must_do token table; `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts` pins the 16-`SKILL.md` `skillTextLines().total` / `totalBytes` (875 lines / 88664 bytes at base) and cross-checks the README measurement cell it must match; `scripts/test-metrics.test.ts` holds the freshness relation; `src/lint/catalog.test.ts` holds the guide and emitted-code assertions; `src/grace-lint.test.ts` holds the mode acceptance and refusal tests. A `SKILL.md` edit moves the footprint pin and the README cell, and both are re-measured with `skillTextLines()` and transcribed, never projected. A new lint code is scanned from its emit site by `collectEmittedIssueCodes` and must resolve to an exact guide through `isEmittableIssueCode`. `grep` each pin before writing scope.

F299 changes the one-suite-run pin on purpose and keeps its intent. The plan must state the predicate's new form and prove the property it protects — each test file executes exactly once per `validate:ci` — with a test, not by widening the predicate to accept anything. The `test:metrics` runner keeps `--reporter=junit` and its non-zero exit on suite failure; no test file is added.

The close's write set is enumerated once. A non-empty `Pays` forces the seven record files under `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/`, the payer-map fixture (`bundleMinted` in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, three entries), the bundle's own archive arrival, and `test-metrics.json`, which moves when a bundle adds a test file: the close's `--assertions final --run-commands` drives `validate:ci`, whose one suite run emits a JUnit report and regenerates the artifact only when the freshness predicate says it is stale. Every one of them is declared in `ObservedWriteScope` and excluded from every byte-invariance pathspec with a reason; the close of a bundle that adds no test file leaves `test-metrics.json` byte-identical.

The four byte-invariance criteria are against base fead8a082646ecbe18e669981833ddcf4661d75f, each a `git diff --exit-code` over one surface with its forced writes excluded: (1) `src/` and `scripts/` minus this bundle's deliverable files; (2) the RM-GOVERNED-PATH non-record roadmap files; (3) `docs/plans/archive/` and `.ngrace/changes/archive/` minus this bundle's own archive arrival (no predecessor archive arrival applies — this is not a supersede); (4) the remaining tracked surfaces minus `package.json`, `test-metrics.json`, `README.md`, the two `SKILL.md` trees, `bun.lock` and the pinned scripts under `scripts/` that are themselves deliverable files. Read exit codes directly, never through a pipe.

Escape markup, never strip it. Where this spec, the plan or a skill must name a tag or angle-bracketed token, write it with entities (`<`, `>`, `&`). Markup-byte assertions belong in a TypeScript test (F43).

Evidence doctrine: probe both directions on a throwaway copy before ratification — the planted F284 escape reddens under `--assertions none` while a clean tree is 0/0; an absent declared path reports the pending warning while a present-unowned file still errors; the chosen F299 path runs the suite once, timed. Red-first with a recorded fail then pass for each guard, one attempt pair per guard. Every `bun test` carries `--timeout=0`. `bun test` green is a precondition, never the evidence.

Do not edit anything under `docs/plans/archive/` or `.ngrace/changes/archive/`; the three archived precedent plans are immutable and are read only. Do not hand-edit `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/` record files; they are written by the retirement move. Do not add an `Assumptions` section to the plan.

NonGoals.NonGoal: F284 shapes not chosen: adding a bare current-mode `ngrace lint` of this root to `validate:ci` (the shape C-REPORT-HONESTY refuses); making `--assertions baseline` or `target` legal without `--change` (contradicts the taught rule that every selected-assertion command names `--change`, F253); and an idle-only check that runs only when no bundle is active (weaker than catching the escape on the pull request). Owner: recorded here; no step.

F297 shapes not chosen: consulting the plan's `DurableScope` anchors as the intended owner of a path that does not exist (weakens A53's LINKS-only stance); treating an absent path as owned without any signal; and any change to archive evaluation. Owner: recorded here; no step.

F299 shapes not chosen: guidance-only wording that renames the count without changing the run (the brief's alternative); dropping `ms` or the slowest-test ranking from the artifact; changing the plain `bun run test` script (the Windows job passes test-file arguments through it); and any change to the JUnit reporter or the untracked-read guard. Owner: recorded here; no step.

`README.md` is a documented surface and this bundle owns it: it gains the `--assertions none` row in the CLI Overview table and corrects the per-test-metrics note so it does not claim a second suite run. Owner: a task of this bundle.

`examples/` is unchanged; no user-visible surface. The new mode and the metrics derivation are CLI, CI and teaching surfaces; `examples/polyglot` neither invokes `--assertions none` nor regenerates `test-metrics.json`, and its active change asserts on files this bundle never writes. Owner: unchanged; no user-visible surface.
No new graph module, no new verification entry, no new `V-M-*` anchor, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, no packaging-version change, and no new test file. Owner: recorded here; no step.
The Windows compatibility job's steps and the `dart-adapter` job's steps do not change; the workflow change is none. Owner: recorded here; no step.
